The Senate's Medicaid reforms in the Bipartisan Health Care Act (S.891) target systemic rot—$71B in annual improper payments and 21M non-citizens straining resources. Sections 101-113 mandate Death Master File checks to purge deceased enrollees and residency verification to stop out-of-state fraud. This isn't "taking healthcare"—it's stopping the theft of taxpayer dollars from veterans and working families.

The bill allocates $10M to audit hospital maternity costs (Section 109), proving we'll fund care efficiently, not endlessly bankroll bureaucratic bloat.

House Republicans should finish the job: protect Americans' safety net by slashing the waste drowning it.
